interpretation: The old baseline observation establishes two concurrent physical fetches and omitted direct usage. This is missing-capability evidence, not a baseline product regression.

Original v1 native record remains 4 failures. Three used immutable snapshot.indexed as an incorrect oracle for current publication. The corrected public Store.search oracle was replayed against the same original library and left one real malformed-usage/restriction regression. No original evidence was rewritten.

V2 passes the original 13 cases (551 checks), 3 supplemental cases (99 checks), and 12 wire/CoreClient/MCP cases (137 checks). ASan/UBSan with detect_leaks=1 replays the same 13+3 scenarios, not new scenarios.

The subsequently approved capacity comparison uses one old-public-API source for both libraries. Baseline passes both cases. V2 fails both with E_JSON_LIMIT after retaining exactly 716800 body bytes. Complete snapshot JSON is 8603131 or 8603477 bytes. One physical fetch served the two failed profile callers.
Therefore passing focused/sanitizer records do not make v2 the final releasable candidate. Capacity repair and appropriate final verification are pending.
Byte integrity verification passed for all 10 closed record groups; an intact failed-run archive remains a failed product observation.
